verdict: Coupling as a geometry probe: the non-additive part of the per-pair coupling delays is NOT explained by an L-array (best corr 0.49, implied pitch 12.6 mm, corner ambiguous): the on-board coupling is not a single free-space path, so a coupling-based per-channel delay calibration is rejected (applying it lowered the scene coherence).

V2 pitch: the joint (pitch x ramp) RA-vs-scaffold grid peaks at pitch 1.4 mm with a removed A-ramp of +70 deg/element (score 0.432, z 1.9 vs azimuth-rolled nulls); pitch and ramp trade off (a ramp = an azimuth shift), so the pitch alone is NOT pinned by this test; the coupling-path pitch estimate (12.6 mm) is physically meaningless (see above).
V4 order/azimuth axis: RA correlation best with azimuth along axis A (corner index 19), score 0.326, z 1.7; runner-up on the other axis: 0.108 (z 1.5)

V6 phases: a deterministic +95 deg/element phase ramp along axis A at every range and frame (per-frame std 3.3 deg); RA-vs-scaffold score vs removed ramp peaks at +70 deg/element (score 0.432; raw 0 deg: -0.006); per-sweep test axis0 similarity 0.56->0.56 (consistency 0.97), axis1 0.56->0.54 (consistency 0.89).

V10 range offset: the coupling peak sits at 10.5 cm range (p5-p95 1.9-27.6), i.e. an on-board electrical path, not a usable zero reference; profile cross-correlation lag vs the rendered scaffold in 0.5-2.6 m: -18.7 cm (corr 0.89).
